scope: GRIM ground truth outside the Wansink/Cornell lab. Covers: (1) Brown & Heathers (2017) GRIM survey and its data requests; (2) Brown & Heathers' work on Nicolas Gueguen and the notices that followed; (3) other named papers with GRIM failures on Nick Brown's blog (all 100 posts read from the Blogger JSON feed, 2007 to 2026-04), James Heathers' Medium posts on Gueguen and GRIM, and Jordan Anaya's GRIMMER preprint; (4) notices and critiques that cite GRIM by name, found through Retraction Watch, Crossref update metadata, PubPeer, Europe PMC full-text search and web search. Compiled 2026-10-17. Every mean_as_printed was copied from a source I read: the article table reproduced as an image on the critic's blog, the notice text, or the critic's own transcription. None comes from memory. Each grim_cells entry was recomputed with a stdlib GRIM check (round-half-up and round-half-even, at the stated n and k); the 'recompute' field gives the result. OSF was down for scheduled maintenance from 2026-10-17 until 2026-10-19 09:00 EDT, so three critic files hosted there could not be read: osf.io/3fcbr (the GRIM project and its list of 260 articles), osf.io/98nzj (Brown & Heathers' 10-article Gueguen report) and osf.io/ngwn8 (the Mueller & Dweck reanalysis). The affected entries say so. The Wansink/Cornell lab is excluded.

papers.title: A bad taste in the mouth: Gustatory disgust influences moral judgment
papers.authors: Eskine, K. J., Kacinik, N. A., & Prinz, J. J.
papers.confirmation_detail: This is one of the 21 articles from the GRIM survey whose authors Brown & Heathers asked for data. The lead author's Gmail address bounced. The dataset (SPSS) later reached Brown through a colleague. It reproduces every Table 1 mean exactly, and shows the condition sizes were swapped in the text: Sweet n = 21 and Water/control n = 18, where the text says Sweet 18 and control 21. The GRIM failures are therefore real against the printed n, and the cause is a reporting error in n. I confirmed this myself by recomputing the means from Brown's posted CSV: Water n = 18 gives 1.1667, 1.3333, 6.6111, 1.8889; Sweet n = 21 gives 1.7619, 5.5238, 1.8095, 1.3810. No correction has been published (Crossref shows no update).

papers.title: Super Size Me: Product Size as a Signal of Status
papers.authors: David Dubois, Derek Rucker, Adam Galinsky
papers.outcome: retracted (2023-10-29), after an expression of concern (2023-06-08)
papers.confirmation_detail: All three authors asked for retraction in October 2022 after Aaron Charlton's report, which included GRIM. The notice: 'retracted following the discovery of a set of statistical errors in studies 1 and 6, which cannot be explained as the authors no longer have the data'. It does not name GRIM. Study 1 is the study that contains the GRIM issues.
papers.grim_cells_not_itemised: Study 1, Table 1: 45 means (9 cells: small/medium/large x coffee/pizza/smoothie; 5 single-item 1-7 DVs each), N = 183, per-cell n unknown (average 20.33). Charlton tested every n from 15 to 25. Share of means that work individually for some n: 82% with regular rounding, 73% with downrounding, 91% mixed. So about 8 of 45 fail at every plausible n under regular rounding. Requiring one n per cell, 40-80% of a cell's 5 means work. The individual failing cells are not named, and his supplement table of means did not survive text extraction from the PDF. Study 3 GRIM issues were explained by the author's habit of downrounding (dataset provided).
papers.other_tests_flagged: Widespread p-value errors; an impossible mediation model in Study 6 (CI asymmetry; c' impossible given a, b, c); Study 2 F test does not reproduce (recomputed F(2,139) = 2.845 vs reported F(1,135) = 10.54); effect-size errors (Ziano et al. replication).
papers.n_question: Cell sizes are not reported, and the author is known to downround (Study 3). Any GRIM label here depends on assumed n and rounding.
papers.notes: Critic is Charlton, not Brown or Heathers. Included under scope item 4 because it is a retraction that followed a GRIM report. A weak target for a cell-level recall benchmark.

searched_but_unusable.what: Brown & Heathers (2017) GRIM survey, SPPS 8(4):363-369, doi 10.1177/1948550616673876: 260 articles (PS, JEP:G, JPSP, 2011-2015), 71 testable, 36 with at least one inconsistent mean (15 rated 1, 5 rated 2, 16 rated 4), 21 data requests, 9 datasets or explanations received.
searched_but_unusable.why: Anonymised by design. The preprint says the authors 'refrained from mentioning the titles, authors or any identifying features', and its footnote 7 says details of the nine datasets were deliberately altered (e.g. 'Sixty' is a changed number). The only article later identified is Eskine et al. (2011) (see papers). A note on the PeerJ preprint page, seen only as a search-result snippet, says the full list of the 260 examined articles was later posted at osf.io/3fcbr; I could not check whether it carries per-article ratings or cells (OSF down until 2026-10-19). Of the 9 datasets: (1) 2 inconsistent means caused by a cell n differing from the column n; (2) the article already had a correction that left most problems unaddressed; (3) Excel formulas selected the wrong cells, and a correction was promised; (4) an early version of the data; (5) Ns from SPSS listwise deletion plus a misreported exclusion count; (6) a misreported total N; (7) wrong dfs and an impossible difference score of 1.5; (8) the author confirmed exclusions were not subtracted from N; (9) missing values and copy errors. None are identifiable.

searched_but_unusable.what: Gueguen (2015) 'High heels increase women's attractiveness', Arch Sex Behav 44:2227-2235, doi 10.1007/s10508-014-0422-z. Retracted 2019-10-11 (10.1007/s10508-019-01558-0).
searched_but_unusable.why: No GRIM claim. Brown's 2017-12-04 post (Study 4) uses SPRITE-style simulation of time-to-approach (a continuous variable) and a wrong F statistic (7.18 vs 8.06-8.16). The notice cites 'serious methodological weaknesses and statistical errors' at the university's request, with no cells.

searched_but_unusable.what: Gueguen (2012) 'Color and women hitchhikers' attractiveness: Gentlemen drivers prefer red', Color Res Appl 37:76-78, doi 10.1002/col.20651.
searched_but_unusable.why: No GRIM claim (N mismatch 5,250 vs 4,800, HSL colours, an impossible inter-rater r). The university agreement required retraction, but Crossref shows no notice as of 2026-10.

searched_but_unusable.what: Gueguen (2015) 'Women's hairstyle and men's behavior', Scand J Psychol 56:637-640, doi 10.1111/sjop.12253. Expression of concern 2022 (10.1111/sjop.12809).
searched_but_unusable.why: No GRIM failure.
